A fine puzzle and construction, I missed the parentheses in the grid but that was a nice touch.

I confess, though, it was just not my bag today. Looking for more of a theme or something more to tie them together; maybe if I appreciated popular music more (I vaguely knew a few of them but none were big nostalgia hits for me except maybe the PINACOLADASONG.) The clues were a mix of gimmes and trivia which I had to deduce from crosses—I don’t mind the trivia so much (I’m willing to be schooled in modern pop culture, such as it is, even Real Housewives) but I would have liked to see at least a few more funny or misdirecting clues.

Got hung up a few places, most specifically the NE-ish area. I really really wanted the Buffy clue to be VAMP ED since it was a handbook, after all. That led me to guess AHMED before ELMER and held me up from getting CELLO and HEAD. And I just couldn’t imagine why you would name (or subtitle) a song “SHES SO HEAVY”— nobody’s going to thank you for that even if it’s slang or idiomatic, lol!

Let’s see, I had TONES before TONYS, that’s on me, and one of my favorite clues. Mitch HEDBURG was one of the few trivia call-outs that I really connected with. And last, just once, I’d like to see “red white and blue land” clue to some other country with a Red White and Blue flag. France? Russia? UK? Ireland? Netherlands? Costa Rica? There’s lots to choose from.

Nice shout-out to Michigan's Grosse Ile--which causes me to reflect--
--the French presence is still quite strong in Detroit, even if mispronounced. For instance, the neighborhood in which I live is bounded by Rivard and St. Aubin Streets, and Lafayette and Gratiot--pronounced GRA-shut--Blvds. (Don't stalk.) Down the street is Chene (SHANE) Park amphitheater (now renamed the Aretha). There are also Nicolet, Joliet, Lasalle, Orleans, Cherboneau, and Chateaufort within spitting distance, and the DeQuindre Cut (a linear park).
Grosse Ile (pronounced Gross Eel, so pretty close) is nowhere near Grosse Pointe--it's downstream in the Detroit River; it is an island, and quite large.
